params.body:
## What

Every page a stranger can reach in this app is a sign-in (`/aanmelden`, the crew's PIN door at `/werf`), a crew screen, or a private share link. None of them is meant to show up in search results.

- `meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"` in the four page shells: the `guest`, `office` and `site` layouts, and the print view.
- `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` in `SecurityHeaders`, so the CSV and Excel exports and the worker photos, which have no head, say the same.
- `robots.txt` is left as it is (`Disallow:` empty). A crawler that is blocked never reads the noindex.

## Why

Elixir scores basic tags on every page it can reach from outside. `/werf` answers 200 without a redirect, so it was scored as a public page with no description, and the project carried an SEO task at 50/100 for a screen nobody should find. Elixir now leaves noindex pages out of that score, so this ends the task at the source rather than in a rule.

## Tests

`SecurityHeadersTest::test_no_page_of_this_app_asks_to_be_found` checks the header and the meta tag on both sign-in routes. The full suite passes: 390 tests.
params.title: Tell search engines the app is not to be found
